newsitem.title: HONG KONG: German faces drugs trial after record seizure in HK.
newsitem.headline: German faces drugs trial after record seizure in HK.

text.p: A Hong Kong court on Monday ordered a German businessman to stand trial for drug smuggling after he was arrested in connection with the record seizure of more than seven tonnes of cannabis in the territory.

Manfred Nelius, 53, who described himself as an importer and exporter of metals, was remanded for two months to face charges of trafficking in dangerous drugs. He will go to trial on December 2, the court ruled.
Nelius was arrested on Saturday. No bail was arranged because Nelius was arrested on a holiday weekend. He was expected to apply for bail of HK$250,000 (US$32,000) later, court sources said.
Under the charge, Nelius was alleged to be the consignee of a cargo of 7.14 tonnes of cannabis worth US$42.4 million that was found in a container terminal.
The shipment was apparently destined for Europe, officials said on Saturday.

"We believe it (originated) from the Golden Triangle area," a senior customs officer said. "We believe the drugs were meant for European countries. I don't know if part of it would be consumed in Hong Kong."
The notorious Golden Triangle is where Thailand, Burma and Laos converge. The official also said an international syndicate was believed to be behind the shipment.
The customs department plans to burn the cannabis.
